packet.headline_seed: Man killed by immigration agent during operation in Maine, official says
packet.description_seed: It comes less than a week after an undocumented migrant was fatally shot in Houston by an immigration agent.

what: Man killed by immigration agent during operation in Maine, official says

clean_source_blocks.text: An ICE agent has fatally shot a motorist in the US state of Maine, a week after an undocumented migrant was killed by a federal immigration officer during a traffic stop in Texas. In the latest incident, Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) said agents were watching an address for a person with a final order of removal in Biddeford at around 07:00 EDT (11:00 GMT) on Monday. When ICE tried to stop a vehicle driven by someone coming from that address, "the vehicle attempted to flee the scene and, fearing for public safety, an officer discharged his weapon", ICE said, adding that "the driver of the vehicle was struck". A 26-year-old Colombian man was shot, immigrant advocates say. ICE did not share details on why the officer feared for safety.
It comes less than a week after an undocumented migrant was fatally shot in Houston by an immigration agent.

Killing of man – identified by rights groups as 26-year-old Colombian – comes days after man killed by ICE in Texas A federal immigration officer shot and killed a man in Biddeford, Maine on Monday, the Department of Homeland Security confirmed, just days ⁠after a man ⁠was ​killed by an immigration officer during a traffic stop in Texas. In the statement, DHS claimed Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers were “conducting targeted surveillance on the last known address of an illegal alien with a final order of removal”. DHS claimed “an illegal alien” left the residence agents were surveilling in a vehicle, which law enforcement “attempted” to stop. It said: “The vehicle attempted to flee the scene and, fearing for public safety, an officer discharged his weapon.”

Fellow Maine Senator Angus King, a political independent, said he was initially told by DHS chief Markwayne Mullin that the person who was shot dead was a target of an arrest warrant in an immigration operation. But hours later, King said Mullin called him to say the man was actually not the target of a warrant, his office told the BBC. According to the Maine Immigrants' Rights Coalition, the person who was killed was a 26-year old Colombian man who was authorised to work in the US. "He was a member of our community, a neighbor, and a human being whose life was cut tragically short," the organisation said in a statement, which did not name the man. "We extend our deepest condolences to his family, loved ones, and everyone now grieving this unimaginable loss."

An ICE agent has fatally shot a motorist in the US state of Maine, a week after an undocumented migrant was killed by a federal immigration officer during a traffic stop in Texas.

In the latest incident, Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) said agents were watching an address for a person with a final order of removal in Biddeford at around 07:00 EDT (11:00 GMT) on Monday.

When ICE tried to stop a vehicle driven by someone coming from that address, "the vehicle attempted to flee the scene and, fearing for public safety, an officer discharged his weapon", ICE said, adding that "the driver of the vehicle was struck".

A 26-year-old Colombian man was shot, immigrant advocates say.

ICE did not share details on why the officer feared for safety.

Maine's top prosecutor said the incident involved an officer from ICE's Enforcement Removal Operations department, and the agent has been placed on leave pending an investigation.

Initial statements indicate "the subject attempted to flee in a vehicle in the direction of the officer and was fatally shot", said Maine's Attorney General Aaron Frey, a Democrat.

The name of the deceased man is not being released until he is formally identified and his family are notified, the statement added.

The inspector general's office for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), which oversees ICE, is taking over the investigation, according to Senator Susan Collins, a Republican representing Maine.

Fellow Maine Senator Angus King, a political independent, said he was initially told by DHS chief Markwayne Mullin that the person who was shot dead was a target of an arrest warrant in an immigration operation.

But hours later, King said Mullin called him to say the man was actually not the target of a warrant, his office told the BBC.

According to the Maine Immigrants' Rights Coalition, the person who was killed was a 26-year old Colombian man who was authorised to work in the US.

"He was a member of our community, a neighbor, and a human being whose life was cut tragically short," the organisation said in a statement, which did not name the man.

"We extend our deepest condolences to his family, loved ones, and everyone now grieving this unimaginable loss."

Protests broke out in Biddeford, 18 miles (30km) south of Portland, following the shooting. Others gathered outside the entrance of Collins' office, to protest against her vote to fund ICE.

payload.title: ICE:n virkailija ampui autoilijan kuoliaaksi Mainessa
payload.summary: ICE:n virkailija ampui 26-vuotiaan kolumbialaismiehen kuoliaaksi Biddefordissa. Viranomaisten mukaan kuljettaja yritti paeta, mutta myöhemmin selvisi, ettei hän ollut operaation varsinainen kohde.
payload.content:
Yhdysvaltain maahanmuutto- ja tullivirasto ICE:n virkailija ampui maanantaina autoilijan kuoliaaksi Biddefordissa Mainen osavaltiossa. Maahanmuuttajien oikeuksia puolustavan järjestön mukaan surmattu oli 26-vuotias kolumbialaismies, jolla oli lupa työskennellä Yhdysvalloissa. Hänen nimeään ei ole kerrottu julkisuuteen.

## Viranomaiset tarkkailivat osoitetta

ICE:n mukaan sen virkailijat tarkkailivat maanantaiaamuna noin kello seitsemältä paikallista aikaa osoitetta, joka oli karkotuspäätöksen saaneen henkilön viimeinen tunnettu asuinpaikka. Yhdysvaltain sisäisen turvallisuuden ministeriö DHS kertoi, että osoitteesta lähti henkilö autolla ja viranomaiset yrittivät pysäyttää ajoneuvon.

Viranomaisten kuvauksen mukaan ajoneuvo yritti paeta paikalta. ICE:n lausunnossa sanottiin virkailijan ampuneen aseellaan, koska hän pelkäsi yleisen turvallisuuden vaarantuvan. Luoti osui kuljettajaan, joka kuoli. ICE ei kertonut, millainen kuljettajan toiminta synnytti turvallisuutta koskeneen pelon, eikä se kuvannut tarkemmin pysäytysyrityksen tapahtumia.

## Surmattu mies ei ollut operaation kohde

Mainen senaattori Angus King kertoi saaneensa aluksi DHS:n johtajalta Markwayne Mullinilta tiedon, että surmattu mies oli maahanmuutto-operaatioon liittyneen pidätysmääräyksen kohde. Kingin toimiston mukaan Mullin soitti hänelle uudelleen muutamaa tuntia myöhemmin ja korjasi tiedon: ammuttu mies ei ollut viranomaisten etsimä henkilö.

Maine Immigrants’ Rights Coalition -järjestö tunnisti surmatun 26-vuotiaaksi kolumbialaismieheksi ja kertoi, että hänellä oli työnteko-oikeus Yhdysvalloissa. Järjestö ei julkistanut hänen nimeään. Lausunnossaan se kuvaili miestä yhteisön jäseneksi, naapuriksi ja ihmiseksi, jonka elämä päättyi traagisesti, sekä esitti surunvalittelunsa hänen perheelleen ja läheisilleen.

## Toinen kuolemantapaus alle viikon sisällä

Biddefordin ampuminen tapahtui alle viikko sen jälkeen, kun liittovaltion maahanmuuttoviranomainen ampui paperittoman siirtolaisen kuoliaaksi liikennepysäytyksen yhteydessä Houstonissa Texasissa. Lähteissä tapausten välille ei ole osoitettu muuta yhteyttä kuin lyhyt ajallinen väli ja maahanmuuttoviranomaisten osallisuus. Mainen tapauksessa avoimeksi jää erityisesti se, mihin virkailijan arvio yleiselle turvallisuudelle aiheutuneesta vaarasta perustui.

article.source_text:
An ICE agent has fatally shot a motorist in the US state of Maine, a week after an undocumented migrant was killed by a federal immigration officer during a traffic stop in Texas. In the latest incident, Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) said agents were watching an address for a person with a final order of removal in Biddeford at around 07:00 EDT (11:00 GMT) on Monday. When ICE tried to stop a vehicle driven by someone coming from that address, "the vehicle attempted to flee the scene and, fearing for public safety, an officer discharged his weapon", ICE said, adding that "the driver of the vehicle was struck". A 26-year-old Colombian man was shot, immigrant advocates say. ICE did not share details on why the officer feared for safety.

It comes less than a week after an undocumented migrant was fatally shot in Houston by an immigration agent.

Killing of man – identified by rights groups as 26-year-old Colombian – comes days after man killed by ICE in Texas A federal immigration officer shot and killed a man in Biddeford, Maine on Monday, the Department of Homeland Security confirmed, just days ⁠after a man ⁠was ​killed by an immigration officer during a traffic stop in Texas. In the statement, DHS claimed Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers were “conducting targeted surveillance on the last known address of an illegal alien with a final order of removal”. DHS claimed “an illegal alien” left the residence agents were surveilling in a vehicle, which law enforcement “attempted” to stop. It said: “The vehicle attempted to flee the scene and, fearing for public safety, an officer discharged his weapon.”

Fellow Maine Senator Angus King, a political independent, said he was initially told by DHS chief Markwayne Mullin that the person who was shot dead was a target of an arrest warrant in an immigration operation. But hours later, King said Mullin called him to say the man was actually not the target of a warrant, his office told the BBC. According to the Maine Immigrants' Rights Coalition, the person who was killed was a 26-year old Colombian man who was authorised to work in the US. "He was a member of our community, a neighbor, and a human being whose life was cut tragically short," the organisation said in a statement, which did not name the man. "We extend our deepest condolences to his family, loved ones, and everyone now grieving this unimaginable loss."
